data.name: Hertha
data.short_meaning: Goddess of fertility and motherly love
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German words ‘heri’ (army) and ‘thu’ (goddess). In Norse mythology, Hertha was a goddess of fertility, protection, and motherly love. In Christianity, Hertha is associated with the Virgin Mary and revered as a patroness of mothers and children.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the nurturing and protective nature of God and the motherly love of the Virgin Mary.
data.numerology_meaning: Indicates new beginnings, leadership, and creativity.

in_hebrew.name: הריטה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הריטה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית ופירושו אדמה או קרקע. השם קשור למושגים של יצירה, התחלה והקשר לאדמה. הוא משמש לעתים קרובות כסמל לחיבור לאדמה ולטבע.

in_greek.name: Χέρτα
in_greek.meaning: Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει γη, έδαφος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χέρτα είναι χριστιανικό και προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα, που σημαίνει γη ή έδαφος. Είναι ένα όνομα που συνδέεται με την έννοια της δημιουργίας και της αρχής, συμβολίζοντας τη σύνδεση με τη γη και τη φύση.

data.cultural_impact: In pre-Christian Germanic cultures, the name Hertha was attributed to the goddess of womanhood, fertility, and protection. Post-Christianization, it evolved to signify devotion, motherhood, and unwavering support. The name maintains a significant connection to the legacy of Germanic mythology and the strong traditions of motherly love and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, Hertha is revered as a patron saint of mothers and children. The name embodies the unwavering love, protection, and nurturing nature of the Virgin Mary, who is believed to intercede on behalf of those who pray to her. Therefore, Hertha, as a Christian name, serves as a constant reminder of the spiritual value of maternal love and loyalty. It exemplifies the deep reverence and connection between the Christian faith and the age-old tradition of the importance of motherhood.
